subject: NimbusData CDN onboarding — subprocessor list and EU→US transfer checklist
messages:
From: Elena Popov <elena@cloudvault.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: subprocessor CSV + dataflow for Nimbus CDN onboarding

Hi Monica / Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier — as discussed, NimbusData is onboarding a new CDN partner (EdgeStream) that will cache static assets and telemetry payloads in multiple regions. Per your DPA requirements, please find the attached exporters list and an initial dataflow sketch.

Quick asks from our side to help the security review:
- Confirm whether Redwood requires SCCs or if you will accept your standard DPA addendum with Equivalency clauses.
- Any specific subprocessor screening questions we should answer beyond SOC 2 + encryption-in-transit?
- Clarify whether telemetry which contains hashed identifiers falls under your EU personal data transfer controls.

Attachment: Nimbus_subprocessors_2026-05-02.csv (text/csv)
Attachment: dataflow_eu_us_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Happy to jump on a short call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Elena Popov
Trust & Compliance Lead
NimbusData Solutions

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Popov <elena@cloudvault.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor CSV + dataflow for Nimbus CDN onboarding

Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear attachments. Quick answers:
- We generally require SCCs for EU→US transfers unless the customer has approved another lawful transfer mechanism. Please flag if your customer contract already contains SCCs.
- Primary screening: SOC 2 Type II (within last 12 months), retention policy, access controls, and whether subprocessors will have access to unredacted PII.
- Hashed identifiers: they may still be considered personal data depending on re-identification risk; Laura (cc) will confirm.

We can accept the attachments for initial review. Laura — can you run the subprocessor CSV through our intake checklist and flag any high-risk entries? If anything is high risk, we may ask Nimbus to exclude that subprocessor or push contractual compensating controls.

Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 May 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: subprocessor CSV + dataflow for Nimbus CDN onboarding

Sooj, forwarding Nimbus's pack — they attached the subprocessor list (CSV) and a rough dataflow. Initial read: EdgeStream (the CDN) is flagged as a new third-party with infrastructure access, and they operate in EU + US.

I ran the CSV through the intake tool: no SOC 2 evidence included for EdgeStream; retention fields are blank. Also a smaller analytics vendor (Tracebit) is listed that retains event logs for 540 days — potential mismatch with our default retention of 90 days for telemetry.

Recommended next steps:
- Ask Nimbus for SOC 2 or equivalent for EdgeStream and Tracebit.
- Confirm SCCs will be executed for EU→US flows OR request that telemetry be pseudonymized to reduce data transfer risk.
- Delay production cutover for EdgeStream until we mark them as low/medium risk.

I suggested a short call with Nimbus security to align expectations. Do you want me to lead the intake ask or should Monica handle front-line?

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Popov <elena@cloudvault.io>, James Corker <james.corker@nimbusdata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 May 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusData CDN onboarding — subprocessor list and EU→US transfer checklist

Elena / James — thanks for the prompt packet and Monica / Laura for the quick triage. A few decisions from Redwood:

1) Before we approve EdgeStream for any customer-facing rollout, Nimbus must provide:
   - SOC 2 Type II report for EdgeStream (last 12 months) or a security questionnaire response acceptable to Redwood.
   - Confirmation that SCCs will be put in place for any EU→US transfers involving telemetry or user identifiers.

2) For Tracebit (analytics): please clarify retention semantics and whether they support shorter retention windows or per-customer retention settings.

3) If Nimbus can provide (a) SOC 2 evidence for the two highlighted subprocessors, and (b) a signed SCC appendix, Redwood can proceed to classify EdgeStream as "low/medium" subject to a 30-day monitoring window post-rollout. If they cannot meet these items, we will request that EdgeStream be excluded from the EU data path and that a non-US CDN be used for EU traffic.

Monica — coordinate the requested evidence. Laura — once we get SOC 2 and SCC confirmation, please update the intake status and push the DocuSign SCC link to the Nimbus deal in HubSpot (link below).

Thanks — I will be available for the call next week if Nimbus prefers a live Q&A.

Soojin Lee
VP, Enterprise Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
